title: How Windows is being optimized for Nvidia's RTX Spark laptops
key_facts: RTX Spark laptops use Arm-based chips with an Nvidia Blackwell GPU and unified memory, so they run x64 Windows apps through Microsoft's Prism emulator, which Microsoft tuned for the chip's design.
A new Get Started experience lets users find, install and open an AI agent in two clicks; agents install and update through the Windows Store.
Hermes, Perplexity and OpenClaw are the first three officially supported agents; the reviewer had trouble setting up OpenClaw and needed a reinstall.
Microsoft ships a Prism compatibility update every month, according to Peter Dawoud, principal program manager at Microsoft.
Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra can have up to 128GB of unified memory; a slider in Nvidia's Windows app sets how much goes to the GPU.

Anti-cheat support is built in for Fortnite, Marvel Rivals, Arc Raiders, Counter-Strike 2 and Dota 2; Call of Duty's Ricochet is due in 2027, Battlefield in early 2027, PUBG in the first half of 2027.
Reviewer's gaming tests: medium settings at 1440p with DLSS performance gave a stable 60fps in most games.
Copilot Plus PC features such as Recall are not available at launch; Microsoft expects them to reach Windows Insiders later this year.
quote_evidence: Emulation isn't generic. Each platform needs tuning.
Surprisingly, Copilot Plus PC features like Recall aren't available on RTX Spark devices at launch.
Large local models are still a lot slower at responding to prompts than cloud models.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows what Microsoft changed in Windows so AI agents and games run on Arm-based Nvidia laptops, and what is still missing.
event_date: Published 15 Oct 2026; based on an Nvidia event the day after the San Francisco launch event of the previous week.
notes: Hands-on report by The Verge's Tom Warren with Microsoft quotes; Microsoft statements are company claims. Follow-up of the 9 Oct launch/price story (C08-02 that day). Viral rule: carried by 20 outlets, score floor 7.
